description.value:
A jagged crack opens in the air, dealing 12d8 cold damage as it draws away warmth. Each creature along the rift must attempt a Fortitude save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.Slowed]{Slowed 1} until the start of your next turn.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage, is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.Immobilized] by a layer of ice, and is slowed 1 as long as it's immobilized. The ice is an object with 60 Hit Points, Hardness 5, immunity to cold damage, and vulnerability 10 to fire. It has object immunities and is destroyed if the target Escapes.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d8 and the ice's Hit Points increase by 5.

You point at a creature and invoke the demise of all things. The target takes 70 void damage with a basic Fortitude save. If the target is undead or otherwise has void healing, the spell loses the death and void traits and gains the vitality trait, and the target takes 70 vitality damage with a basic Fortitude save.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 10.

You can ask questions of and receive answers from natural or worked stone. While stone is not intelligent, you speak with the natural spirits of the stone, which have a personality colored by the type of stone, as well as by the type of structure the stone is part of, for worked stone. A stone's perspective, perception, and knowledge give it a worldview different enough from a human's that it doesn't consider the same details important. Stones can mostly answer questions about creatures that touched them in the past and what is concealed beneath or behind them.

Heightened (6th) The duration is 8 hours.

You conjure a poisonous fog. This functions as @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Mist], except the area moves 10 feet away from you each round. You deal 6d8 poison damage to each breathing creature that starts its turn in the spell's area. You can Dismiss the spell.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d8.

You sculpt an ice barrier that blocks sight and, once shattered, freezes foes. You create either a 1-foot-thick wall of ice in a straight line up to 60 feet long and 10 feet high (the wall doesn't have to be vertical, but it must be anchored on both sides to a solid surface) or a 1-foot-thick, 10-foot radius hemisphere of ice. The ice that makes up the wall is opaque. If you wish, the wall can be of a smaller length, height, or radius.

You must create the wall in an unbroken open space so its edges don't pass through any creatures or objects, or the spell is lost. Each 10-foot-by-10-foot section of the wall has AC 10, Hardness 10, and 40 Hit Points, and it's immune to critical hits, cold damage, and precision damage. A section also has weakness 15 to fire; a section of the wall destroyed by fire melts, evaporating into water and steam. A section destroyed by means other than fire leaves behind a chilling mass of ice that is difficult terrain and deals 2d6 cold damage to any creature passing through it.

Heightened (+2) The Hit Points of each section of the wall increase by 10, and the cold damage dealt to creatures crossing a destroyed section increases by 1d6.

You can ask questions of and receive answers from plants and fungi, but the spell doesn't make them more friendly or intelligent than normal. Most normal plants and fungi have a distinctive view of the world around them, so they don't recognize details about creatures or know anything about the world beyond their immediate vicinity. Cunning plant or fungus monsters are likely to be terse and evasive, while less intelligent ones often make inane comments.

Heightened (4th) The duration is 8 hours.

Your touch leeches the lifeblood out of a target to empower yourself. You deal 6d6 void damage to the target. You gain temporary Hit Points equal to half the void damage the target takes (after applying resistances and the like). You lose any remaining temporary Hit Points after 1 minute.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 2d6.

You can ask questions of, receive answers from, and use the Diplomacy skill with animals. The spell doesn't make them more friendly than normal. Cunning animals are likely to be terse and evasive, while less intelligent ones often make inane comments.

In your mind's eye, you magically reorient yourself. You immediately know which direction is north (if it exists at your current location), and you can choose a location you were at within the last 24 hours and learn what direction it lies.

Heightened (3rd) You can choose a location you were at within the last week.

Heightened (7th) You can choose a location you were at regardless of how long ago you were there.

This projectile weapon is made from horn, wood, and sinew laminated together to increase the power of its pull and the force of its projectile. Like all longbows, its great size also increases the bow's range and power. You must use two hands to fire it, and it cannot be used while mounted. Any time an ability is specifically restricted to a longbow, such as Erastil's favored weapon, it also applies to composite longbows unless otherwise stated.
A mix of flexible and molded boiled leather, a suit of this type of armor provides some protection with maximum flexibility.
The wild hunt archer ignores the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.Concealed] condition from leaves and other foliage.
The wild hunt archer treats the plane it is located on as its home plane.

500 feet. Other wild hunt creatures in the area, except wild hunt archers, automatically succeed at their flat checks to target @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.Concealed] creatures with ranged Strikes.
@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.ConstantSpells]
The wild hunt archer automatically critically succeeds at saving throws against effects created by allied wild hunt creatures.

30 feet. Those who meet the gaze of a wild hunt archer are overwhelmed by the pressure of the hunt's legacy. A creature that ends its turn in the emanation must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:34] save or be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.Slowed]{Slowed 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.Slowed]{Slowed 2} on a critical failure) until it leaves. The wild hunt hound can deactivate or activate this aura with a single action, which has the concentrate trait.

The wild hunt archer fixes its glare on a creature it can see within 30 feet, which must immediately save against wild gaze. A creature that fails its save and was already slowed by wild gaze is instead @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.Paralyzed] for 1 round, after which it is immune to Focus Gaze from any wild hunt creature until the start of the wild hunt hound's next turn.

The wild hunt archer Casts a Spell that requires a saving throw and makes a living bow Strike, imbuing the spell's effects into the arrow. If the Strike hits a creature, the spell targets that creature or centers its area on that creature, even if it would normally be out of the spell's range, and the creature struck takes a –2 circumstance penalty to its save against the spell's effect. If the Strike misses, the spell is wasted.

The wild hunt archer's bow is a manifestation of their skill that comes alive in their hands. While the wild hunt archer wields it, the living bow becomes a +2 greater striking frost composite longbow and spontaneously manifests arrows of primal energy. If the bow is lost or destroyed, a wild hunt archer can manifest a replacement living bow by concentrating for 1 minute.
The wild hunt archer's ranged Strikes ignore the target's @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.Concealed] condition.

languages.details: speak with animals; speak with plants

details.publicNotes:
Wild hunt archers are androgynous humanoids have glowing green eyes, pointed ears, horns, and hair that always flows softly as if in a gentle breeze. Since they tend to be slower on foot than most of their companions, they often rely on their mounts for increased mobility. They carry no arrows, instead producing them from magical quivers that function only for them. Their bows are made of living wood.

Although some believe the wild hunt is nothing more than legend, the riders of the hunt are very real, comprised of countless lithe, horned humanoids, along with their steeds and hunting hounds. The term "wild hunt" refers to these fey as a whole, as well as to individual groups who gather at a wild hunt monarch's call to pursue their chosen quarry. The less dangerous a quarry, the more likely a monarch will impose rules to make the hunt more entertaining.
